verdict_reason: _isoscore reproduces the RELEASED IsoScore 2.0.1 package (installed here) on the same clouds: isotropic gaussian 2000x64 BLME 0.9667461859774082 vs official 0.9667461841527681 (rel 1.89e-09), rank-8-in-R^64 rel 2.64e-07, extreme-anisotropy rel 1.52e-05 -- and in that last case BLME is the more accurate of the two, because the official route squares the data into torch.cov before the SVD while BLME takes the SVD of the centered matrix and squares afterwards. The algebra matches Rudman et al. Eq. 4.1 term for term (eigenvalues padded to d, L2-normalised to sqrt(d), defect = ||sigma_hat - 1||/sqrt(2(d-sqrt(d))), score = ((d - delta^2(d-sqrt(d)))^2 - d)/(d(d-1))). tests/test_scale_invariance.py::test_isoscore_is_scale_invariant and ::test_isoscore_is_translation_invariant pass; I re-measured translation at +1e6 in float32 storage and got 0.9316587816 against the float64 truth 0.9316797579 (rel 2.25e-05, the same order as the official's own 1.83e-05).
comparable_reason: Raw isoscore carries a structural 1/(d-1) factor: rho -0.433 with d_model (p=2.8e-04) and -0.463 with log-params (p=9.1e-05) over the 66-model archive. The zero-padding isometry makes the mechanism explicit -- embedding the SAME 8-dimensional cloud in d = 64/256/1024/4096 moves the raw score 0.110955 -> 0.027412 -> 0.006833 -> 0.001707, a factor of 65, purely from the ambient dimension.
normalized_ok_detail: It works, and it is the only normalizer on this campaign that passes the mechanism test outright. Under the same d = 64 -> 4096 zero-padding isometry it holds 7.990170056143993 / 7.990170056143993 / 7.990170056143962 / 7.9901700561439215 -- unchanged to 8.4e-15 while the raw score moves 65x. On the archive its d_model association collapses from rho -0.433 (p=2.8e-04) to -0.089 (p=0.48). I also confirmed the documented identity: iso*(d-1)+1 IS the covariance participation ratio (sum lam)^2/sum(lam^2) to rel 0.000e+00 / 7.8e-16 / 2.2e-16 on three clouds, so it must not enter a feature matrix alongside geometry_svd.participation_ratio.
github_reason: The official package is installed on this host. I read IsoScore.IsoScore's source (torch.cov -> svdvals -> pcs*sqrt(n)/||pcs|| -> defect -> rescale) and ran it head-to-head against _isoscore on four clouds; worst relative disagreement 1.52e-05, on the case where the official's cov-then-SVD route loses the precision. BLME's only deliberate departures are the float64 promotion, the S/S[0] rescale (both exactly cancelling) and a [0,1] clamp the reference lacks.
paper_reason: Rudman et al.'s defining anchors reproduce: an isotropic Gaussian at n >> d scores 0.9667 (paper: -> 1 as n -> inf; the finite-N floor at this (n,d) is 0.9668, so the value is AT the floor), and an 8-dimensional cloud embedded in d ambient dimensions scores (k/d - 1/d)/(1 - 1/d) exactly -- 0.110955 at d=64 against the closed form 0.111111 (0.14%) and 0.0017070 at d=4096 against 0.00170898 (0.11%).
confounds_reason: Raw isoscore rho -0.433 with d_model (p=2.8e-04), -0.310 with n_layers, -0.463 with log-params over 66 models, and the zero-padding isometry shows the association is the structural 1/(d-1) factor rather than any property of the representations. isoscore_effective_dims removes it (rho -0.089, p=0.48) and its measured range over the archive is 1.17 to 165.80, so the width dependence is gone but the VALUE genuinely varies -- as the source's own 2026-09-04 correction says.
